items.title: Heavy chiral U(1)_V threshold model data
items.design_state: Defines the exact selected H=SU(3)×U(1)_V heavy-chiral threshold model, singlet charge, Yukawa mass, regulator, counterterm convention, and source-backed mass-independent threshold input.
items.physical_scope: A selected perturbative U(1)_V-singlet chiral threshold sector inside H=SU(3)×U(1)_V on the trivial bundle over four-dimensional Minkowski space; no dynamical gauge-consistency or global-anomaly claim.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ on the four-dimensional affine Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, as in the selected HEFT spacetime convention. Use the trivial spin structure, spinor bundle $S=M\times\mathbb C^4$, gamma matrices satisfying $\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}I$, chirality operator $\gamma_5=i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3$, and eigensubbundles $S_\pm=\ker(\gamma_5\mp I)$. Take the trivial bundle for the fixed global symmetry group $H=SU(3)\times U(1)_V$, set the $SU(3)$ background connection to zero, and keep only the nondynamical $U(1)_V$ connection $B\in\Omega_c^1(M,\mathbb R)$ with curvature $G=dB$. Here $U(1)_V=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ and its charge-$q$ representation is $\rho_q(z)=z^q$ on $\mathbb C$. The background $B$ is not integrated over as a quantum gauge redundancy.

Let $\psi_+\in C_c^\infty(M,S_+\otimes\mathbb C_{(\mathbf1,+1)})$ and $\psi_-\in C_c^\infty(M,S_-\otimes\mathbb C_{(\mathbf1,0)})$ be complex Weyl fields in the indicated $SU(3)\times U(1)_V$ representations. Use $D_q=d+iqB$ on charge-$q$ fields and the fixed Lorentz-scalar chiral Dirac pairing $\bar\psi_+\psi_-$. Let $\Phi=v e^{i\theta}$ be a nonvanishing order-parameter field in $(\mathbf1,+1)$ with fixed modulus $v>0$ and smooth real phase $\theta\in C_c^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$. A dimensionless nonzero Yukawa parameter $y$ gives the mass term $-y\Phi\bar\psi_+\psi_-+\mathrm{h.c.}$, where h.c. denotes Hermitian conjugation, and heavy mass $M_H=|y|v>0$. The fermion fields have mass dimension $3/2$, $v$ and $M_H$ have mass dimension one, $B_\mu$ has mass dimension one, $G_{\mu\nu}$ has mass dimension two, and $\theta$ is dimensionless.

For $\alpha\in C_c^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$, use $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$, $\psi_+\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\psi_+$, $\psi_-\mapsto\psi_-$, and $\Phi\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\Phi$, hence $\theta\mapsto\theta-\alpha$. These transformations leave the Yukawa term invariant. In the anti-Hermitian product-group convention, the selected singlet has connection $iB$ and covariant derivative $d+iB$; in Bilal's Hermitian convention write $\mathscr A=-B$ and $\epsilon=-\alpha$, so $d-i\mathscr A=d+iB$ and the transformations agree. Let $\Gamma_H[B,\theta]$ denote the formal one-loop effective-action contribution of this fermion pair with the Pauli–Villars subtraction used for the chiral triangle: include a physical loop with $M_0=0$ and three regulator loops with statistics weights $\eta_0=\eta_2=1$ and $\eta_1=\eta_3=-1$, choose a positive scale $M_{\mathrm{PV}}$ and masses $M_1=M_3=M_{\mathrm{PV}}$, $M_2=\sqrt2M_{\mathrm{PV}}$, and take $M_{\mathrm{PV}}\to\infty$ after the subtraction. Define the consistent anomaly as the infinitesimal variation of this effective action, rather than as a covariant-current divergence. Add no non-invariant local counterterm to $\Gamma_H$; gauge-invariant local counterterms may be added. For an undetermined real coefficient $c$, the candidate Wess–Zumino functional is $\Gamma_c[B,\theta]=c\int_M\theta G\wedge G$; the theorem on this page fixes $c$.

As a source-backed threshold input, adopt the following scope-limited consequence of the heavy-fermion field-redefinition argument: removing the phase of a Yukawa-generated heavy chiral mass by a chiral redefinition transfers that phase to the regulated measure, whose consistent anomalous variation is independent of the heavy mass. This supplies the local Wess–Zumino threshold interpretation when $\theta$ is retained; it is not a construction of the full determinant or a bound on all remaining terms. Let $E$ be a positive mass scale bounding absolute external momentum components in these coordinates. The threshold regime is $E/M_H\ll1$, with no Lorentz-invariant norm or expansion-remainder bound asserted. All determinant and anomaly data here are formal perturbative inputs; no exact functional integral or continuum limit is claimed.

items.title: Heavy-chiral threshold Wess–Zumino anomaly match
items.design_state: Derives the local consistent-anomaly Wess–Zumino matching relation for the selected charge-one U(1)_V singlet and fixes the Hermitian-convention sign explicitly.
items.physical_scope: Perturbative local anomaly matching for one positive-chirality SU(3)-singlet, U(1)_V-charge-one Weyl field, one neutral negative-chirality mass partner, and a retained charge-one Goldstone phase under small background U(1)_V transformations. It asserts no dynamical-gauge consistency, large-transformation/global anomaly, gravitational term, non-Abelian generalization, or continuum limit.
items.statement:
On natural-unit Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, take the trivial $H=SU(3)\times U(1)_V$ bundle, zero $SU(3)$ background, and a smooth compactly supported real nondynamical $U(1)_V$ connection $B$ with $G=dB$. Let $\alpha,\theta\in C_c^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$. Use one smooth compactly supported positive-chirality Weyl field in $(\mathbf1,+1)$, one smooth compactly supported neutral negative-chirality mass partner, and the charge-one scalar $\Phi=v e^{i\theta}$ in the Yukawa term $-y\Phi\bar\psi_+\psi_-+\mathrm{h.c.}$, where $v>0$, $y\ne0$, and $M_H=|y|v$. Fix the transformations $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$, $\psi_+\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\psi_+$, $\psi_-\mapsto\psi_-$, and $\theta\mapsto\theta-\alpha$, and use the consistent-anomaly representative with no non-invariant local counterterm. Let $E$ bound absolute external momentum components in these coordinates and assume $E/M_H\ll1$.

Adopt the source-derived consistent-anomaly formula for a positive-chirality Weyl field in representation $R$, written in Bilal's Hermitian convention,

$$\delta_{\epsilon}\Gamma_R=-\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M\operatorname{tr}_R\!\left(\epsilon\,d\left(\mathscr A\wedge d\mathscr A-\frac{i}{2}\mathscr A\wedge\mathscr A\wedge\mathscr A\right)\right).$$

For the selected $U(1)_V$ representation, set $\mathscr A=-B$ and $\epsilon=-\alpha$, so $d-i\mathscr A=d+iB$ and the positive-chirality field transforms as specified above. Since $R=(\mathbf1,+1)$ is one-dimensional, $\operatorname{tr}_R(1)=1$; since $\mathscr A$ is Abelian, its cubic wedge term vanishes. The heavy-sector local variation is therefore $\mathcal A_H(\alpha,B)=+\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M\alpha G\wedge G$. If $\Gamma_L$ is any specified remaining-light-sector functional with infinitesimal variation $\mathcal A_L$, and the low-energy theory retains $\theta$ and is required to match this perturbative background anomaly, then

$$\Gamma_{\mathrm{WZ}}[B,\theta]=-\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M\theta G\wedge G$$

satisfies $\delta_\alpha\Gamma_{\mathrm{WZ}}=\mathcal A_H$ and hence $\delta_\alpha(\Gamma_L+\Gamma_{\mathrm{WZ}})=\mathcal A_L+\mathcal A_H=\delta_\alpha(\Gamma_L+\Gamma_H)$. Its coefficient has no $M_H^{-1}$ factor. This is a local perturbative anomaly-matching statement in the fixed representative; it asserts no global determinant phase, dynamical-gauge consistency, gravitational contribution, non-Abelian generalization, convergence of the EFT expansion, or continuum interacting QFT.

items.title: Compactly supported background with a nonzero heavy-fermion anomaly variation
items.design_state: Evaluates the theorem on one normalized smooth compactly supported U(1)_V background and obtains a nonzero exact local variation.
items.physical_scope: A fixed smooth compactly supported background-field calculation inside the perturbative local U(1)_V threshold model; it is illustrative and makes no empirical or global-anomaly claim.
items.statement: In the trivial-bundle $H=SU(3)\times U(1)_V$ threshold model on natural-unit Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and zero $SU(3)$ background, use a smooth real compactly supported $U(1)_V$ potential $B$ and parameter $\alpha$, with $G=dB$ and $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$, $\theta\mapsto\theta-\alpha$. Choose a smooth compactly supported cutoff $\chi$ that equals $1$ on a neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}\alpha$, with $\alpha\geq0$. Let $\lambda>0$ have mass dimension two and set $B=\lambda\chi(x)(x^0dx^1+x^2dx^3)$, normalizing $\alpha$ so that $\lambda^2\int_M\alpha\,d^4x=1$. For the charge-one positive-chirality field, neutral mass partner, and heavy mass $M_H$ of the stated model, choose the external scale $E$ in the regime $E/M_H\ll1$. Then the consistent heavy-sector variation and the Wess–Zumino variation are equal, nonzero, and each equals $+1/(12\pi^2)$.
